text:
If the sum of the second, third and fourth terms
of a positive term G.P. is 3 and the sum of its
sixth, seventh and eighth terms is 243, then the
sum of the first 50 terms of this G.P. is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let first term = a > 0

Common ratio = r > 0

$ar + ar^{2}$
 $+ ar^{3}$
 = 3 ....(i)

$ar^{5}$
 $+ ar^{6}$
 $+ ar^{7}$
 = 243 ....(ii)

$\Rightarrow$ $r^{4}(ar + ar^{2} + ar^{3}) = 243$

$\Rightarrow$ $r^{4}(3) = 243$ 

$\Rightarrow$ r = 3 as r > 0

from (i)

3a + 9a + 27a = 3

$\Rightarrow$ a = $\frac{1}{13}$

$\therefore$ $S_{50} =$ $\frac{a\left (r^{50}-1\right )}{(r-1)}$

= $\frac{1}{26}\left (3^{50}-1\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
If a + x = b + y = c + z + 1, where a, b, c, x, y, z

are non-zero distinct real numbers, then

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} x & a+y & x+a \\ y & b+y & y+b \\ z & c+y & z+c \end{array}\right |$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left |\begin{array}{lll} x & a+y & x+a \\ y & b+y & y+b \\ z & c+y & z+c \end{array}\right |$

$C_{3}$ $\to$ $C_{3} – C_{1}$

= $\left |\begin{array}{lll} x & a+y & a \\ y & b+y & b \\ z & c+y & c \end{array}\right |$

$C_{2}$ $\to$ $C_{2} – C_{3}$

= $\left |\begin{array}{lll} x & y & a \\ y & y & b \\ z & y & c \end{array}\right |$

$R_{3}$ $\to$ $R_{3} – R_{1}, R_{2}$ $\to$ $R_{2} – R_{1}$

= $\left |\begin{array}{lll} x & y & a \\ y-x & 0 & b-a \\ z-x & 0 & c-a \end{array}\right |$

= (–y)[(y – x) (c – a) – (b – a) (z – x)]

Given, a + x = b + y = c + z + 1

=  (–y)[(a – b) (c – a) + (a – b) (a – c – 1)]

= (–y)[(a – b) (c – a) + (a – b) (a – c) + b – a)

= –y(b – a) = y(a – b)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential
equation

cosx$\frac{dy}{dx}$ + 2ysinx = sin2x, x $\in$ $\left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$.

If
y$\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )$ = 0, then y$\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
cosx$\frac{dy}{dx}$ + 2ysinx = sin2x

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dy}{dx}+2y\tan x=2\sin x$

I.F = $e^{\int 2\tan xdx}$ $= \sec ^{2} x$

$y.\sec ^{2} x =$ $\int 2\sin x\sec ^{2}xdx$

$\Rightarrow$ ysec$^{2}x =$ $\int 2\tan x\sec xdx$

$\Rightarrow$ ysec$^{2}x = 2$secx + c

Given at x = $\frac{π}{3}$, y = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 0 = $2\sec \frac{π}{3}+c$

$\Rightarrow$ c = -4

ysec$^{2}x = 2$secx - 4

Here put x = $\frac{π}{4}$

y.2 = $2\sqrt{2}$ - 4

$\Rightarrow$ y = $\sqrt{2}-2$

text:
If the mean and the standard deviation of the

data 3, 5, 7, a, b are 5 and 2 respectively, then
a and b are the roots of the equation :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mean = $\frac{3+5+7+a+b}{5}$ = 5

$\Rightarrow$ $a$ + b = 10

Variance = $\frac{3^{2}+5^{2}+7^{2}+a^{2}+b^{2}}{5}$ $- (5)^{2} = 4$

$\Rightarrow$ $a^{2}+b^{2}$ = 62

$\Rightarrow$ $(a+b)^{2}-2ab$ = 62

$\Rightarrow$ $ab$ = 19

So $a$ and b are the roots of the equation

$x^{2} – 10x + 19 = 0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
If x = 1 is a critical point of the function

$f(x) = (3x^{2}$
 $+ ax – 2 – a)e^{x}$
, then :
options:
x = 1 is a local maxima and x = $-\frac{2}{3}$ is a
local minima of f.
x = 1 and x = $-\frac{2}{3}$ are local maxima of f.
x = 1 and x = $-\frac{2}{3}$ are local minima of f.

x = 1 is a local minima and x = $-\frac{2}{3}$ is a local
maxima of f.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x) = (3x^{2}$
 $+ ax – 2 – a)e^{x}$

$\therefore$ $f'(x) = e^{x}(6x + a) + (3x^{2}$
 $+ ax – 2 – a)e^{x}$

 $= e^{x}(3x^{2} + x(6 + a) – 2)$

f '(x) = 0 at x = 1

$\Rightarrow$ 3 + (6 + a) – 2 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ a = -7

$\therefore$  $f'(x) = e^{x}(3x^{2} – x – 2)$

$= e^{x}(x – 1) (3x + 2)$

[IMG]


x = 1 is a local minima and x = $-\frac{2}{3}$ is a local
maxima of f.

If the length of the chord of the circle,

$x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}$
 (r > 0) along the line, y – 2x = 3 is r,

then $r^{2}$
 is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


In right $\Delta$CDB,

$\sin  60^{o} =$ $\frac{CD}{r}$

$\Rightarrow$ CD = $r\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ = $\frac{\sqrt{3}r}{2}$

Now equation of AB is

y – 2x – 3 = 0

So $\frac{\sqrt{3}r}{2}$ = $\frac{|0+0-3|}{\sqrt{5}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\sqrt{3}r}{2}$ = $\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}$

$\Rightarrow$ r = $\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ $r^{2} =$ $\frac{12}{5}$

text:
If the system of linear equations

x + y + 3z = 0

$x + 3y + k^{2}z = 0$

3x + y + 3z = 0

has a non-zero solution (x, y, z) for some k $\in$ R,
then x + $\left (\frac{y}{z}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
x + y + 3z = 0 .....(i)

$x + 3y + k^{2}z = 0  .........(ii)$

3x + y + 3z = 0 ......(iii)

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & k^{2} \\ 3 & 1 & 3 \end{array}\right |$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $9 + 3 + 3k^{2}$
$– 27 – k^{2}$
– 3 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $k^{2} = 9$

Perform (i) – (iii),

–2x = 0 $\Rightarrow$ x = 0

Now from (i),  y + 3z = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{y}{z}=-3$

$\therefore$ x + $\left (\frac{y}{z}\right )$ = -3

text:
If

$\int \frac{\cos θ}{5+7\sin θ-2\cos ^{2}θ}dθ$ = A$\log _{e}|B(θ)|+C$,

where C is a constant of integration, then $\frac{B(θ)}{A}$

can be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int \frac{\cos θ}{5+7\sin θ-2\cos ^{2}θ}dθ$

= $\int \frac{\cos θdθ}{5+7\sin θ-2\left (1-\sin ^{2}θ\right )}$

= $\int \frac{\cos θdθ}{3+7\sin θ+2\sin ^{2}θ}$

Let sin $θ$ = t

$\Rightarrow$ cos$θ$d$θ$ = dt

= $\int \frac{dt}{3+7t+2t^{2}}$

= $\int \frac{dt}{(2t+1)(t+3)}$

= $\frac{1}{5}\int \left (\frac{2}{2t+1}-\frac{1}{t+3}\right )dt$

= $\frac{1}{5}\ln \left |\frac{2t+1}{t+3}\right |$ + C

= $\frac{1}{5}\ln \left |\frac{2\sin θ+1}{\sin θ+3}\right |$ + C

$\therefore$ A = $\frac{1}{5}$ and B($θ$) = $\frac{2\sin θ+1}{\sin θ+3}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{B(θ)}{A}$ = $\frac{5(2\sin θ+1)}{\sin θ+3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
Let A = {a, b, c} and B = {1, 2, 3, 4}. Then the
number of elements in the set 
C = {f : A $\to$ B |
2 $\in$ f(A) and f is not one-one} is $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The desired functions will contain either one
element or two elements in its codomain of
which '2' always belongs to f(A).

Case 1 : When 2 is the image of all element of set A.

Number of ways this is possible  = 1

Case 2 : When one image is 2 and other one image is one of {1, 3, 4}.

Number of ways we can choose one of {1, 3, 4} is $= ^{3}C_{1}$.

Now divide 3 elements {a, b, c} of set A into two parts.

We can do this $\frac{3!}{2!1!}$ ways.

Now map one part of set A into the element 2 of set B and map other part of set A into one of {1, 3, 4} of set B.

We can do that 2! ways.

So number of functions in this case 

$= ^{3}C_{1}$ $\times$ $\frac{3!}{2!1!}$ $\times$ 2! = 18

$\therefore$ Total number of functions = 1 + 18 = 19
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
Let the vectors $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$
 be such that

$\left |\vec{a}\right |=2$, $\left |\vec{b}\right |=4$
 and $\left |\vec{c}\right |=4$. If the projection of

$\vec{b}$
 on $\vec{a}$
 is equal to the projection of $\vec{c}$
 on $\vec{a}$

and $\vec{b}$
 is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$,
 then the value of

$\left |\vec{a}+⃗{b}-\vec{c}\right |$
 is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Projection of $\vec{b}$
 on $\vec{a}$
= Projection of $\vec{c}$
 on $\vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\vec{b}.\vec{a}}{\left |\vec{a}\right |}=\frac{\vec{c}.\vec{a}}{\left |\vec{a}\right |}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{b}.\vec{a}=\vec{c}.\vec{a}$

$\because$ $\vec{b}$
 is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{b}.\vec{c}=0$

Let $\left |\vec{a}+⃗{b}-\vec{c}\right |$ = k

Square both sides

$k^{2} =$ $\left (\vec{a}\right )^{2}$ + $\left (\vec{b}\right )^{2}$ + $\left (\vec{c}\right )^{2}$ + $2\vec{a}.\vec{b}$ - $2\vec{b}.\vec{c}$ - $2\vec{a}.\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow$ $k^{2} =$ $\left (\vec{a}\right )^{2}$ + $\left (\vec{b}\right )^{2}$ + $\left (\vec{c}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $k^{2} = 2^{2} + 4^{2} + 4^{2} = 36$

$\Rightarrow$ k = 6
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot
